note: Rewritten from Light 1932, pp. 385—387; original in English; known only from the alate, the soldier and worker being unknown (the original lists it under "Species based on alates and not placed by group"); the measurements are of a single individual.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Only the alate is known, the soldier being unknown. Alate very pale: head pale brown; pronotum, wing scales, meso- and metanotal tergites and thoracic sclerites pale rusty brown; postclypeus, labrum, antennae, palps, legs, ventral thoracic sclerites and abdominal sternites yellow; abdominal tergites very pale yellowish brown. Small, only 9.5 mm long including the wings; head width about 1 mm. The author notes that it can be distinguished with the naked eye from all other known alates of the genus by its very pale colour. It is the species that Banks (1920) mistakenly identified as the alate of his A. californicus. The size of the ocelli and the pigmentation of the fontanelle vary: when the ocelli are smaller they are almost circular and stand about their short diameter from the eye; the fontanelle is pigmented to varying degrees and is sometimes pigmented throughout except for the bracket-shaped white area in front, in which case it forms a shallow Y with the frontal line.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head as in the original fig. R: sides strongly receding posteriorly, passing broadly and roundly into the convex posterior margin; widest in front of the eyes; head low, lowest behind and highest slightly in front of the level of the ocelli. Fontanelle large, conspicuously white, broadly oval to triangular; broad in front, more or less extensively pigmented behind; frons with a narrow bracket-shaped white band; in front of this a short white or yellow line. Muscle impressions faint; median suture distinct posteriorly. Postclypeus more than twice as wide as long; anterior margin broad and very shallowly concave; slightly swollen. Eyes round, flat; separated from the dorsal and ventral margins of the head by more than half their diameter and from the posterior margin of the head by about twice their diameter. Ocelli short-oval; length about half the eye diameter; close to the eyes, less than half their short diameter away. Antennae rather long, 15-segmented; segment 3 smallest. Pronotum (original fig. S) small, narrower than the head width between the eyes, about twice as wide as long; anterior margin straight or slightly concave; widest near the front; anterior corners very short and rounded; sides convex, converging, passing broadly and roundly into the weakly biconvex posterior margin. Measurements (mm): length including wings 9.50; forewing length 7.00; head length including the labrum 1.20; head capsule length 0.74; head width across the eyes 0.99; eye length 0.23; ocellus length 0.12; ocellus width 0.09; postclypeus length 0.20; postclypeus width 0.46; pronotum length 0.42; pronotum width 0.72; postclypeus index 0.44.
